newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK, Richter seen top earners.
newsitem.headline: TVK, Richter seen top earners.

text.p: Hungary's stock market, more or less discounting earnings hopes, expects chemical firm TVK and pharmaceutical Richter to highlight a mixed batch of first-half results of bourse-listed companies.
"Probably TVK will have the most outstanding earnings, as a result of the fact that the chemical cycle favours the company," said Robert Feuer, analyst at WestMerchant in London.
Market talk says that TVK's first-half earnings will match or even exceed last year's annual IAS after-tax profit of 7.69 billion forints.
The company's fortunes might change, however, if margins between its main raw material naptha and its output ethylene narrow later this year or next year, as expected by analysts.

Earnings hopes are more moderate about the market's other chemical stock BorsodChem which uses ethylene as raw material, therefore the chemicals cycle had the opposite impact than on TVK, analysts said.

But BorsodChem's other product, the methylene-diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) which accounts for almost half of BorsodChem's profits while its proportion within its sales is smaller, will be at hand to offset, they said.
"BorsodChem's earnings are less volatile (than those of TVK) due to a more diversifed product range," Feuer said.
Recent price rises have more or less reflected this difference between the two firms, when comparing the change between their closing prices at the end of March and the end of June.
BorsodChem's price grew 15 percent to 7,495 forints at the end of June from 6,520 at the end of March, while TVK registered a 47 percent rise from 2,225 forints to 3,270.

More substantial is the change when including July as well and comparing July 23 closing prices of 7,395 forints and 3,920 forints, respectively, to end of March. BorsodChem gave up some, showing only a 13.4 percent rise, while TVK powered ahead to post a 76 percent gain in price.

Analysts are hopeful on pharmaceuticals maker Richter Gedeon, while they do not expect a positive surprise from peer company Egis Gyogyszergyar which earlier confirmed a recent press report which said that trends in the second quarter did not bring change compared to the first.

"We expect Richter to boost its total sales by an annualised 11 percent in dollar terms," said Ferenc Szollosi, analyst at Postabank Securities. "The continuous strengthening of the dollar will be reflected by the forint figures."

In a strong first quarter of 1997, Richter reported its total sales rising 11.4 percent in dollar terms to $74.5 million over the first three months of 1996, with sales to the CIS firming 40.1 percent to $22.7 million.
Exports have traditionally accounted for around two-thirds of Richter's total sales and most exports are invoiced in dollars.
Differences between Richter's and Egis's price reflect the different earnings growth prospects, with Richter closing at 18,500 forints and Egis at 12,750 forints on Wednesday.
